title: Does the harvest yield make farm tools affordable soon enough?
question:
Harvest-as-seed is live: a harvested wheat or tomato is the same unit the player plants again, and the starter wheat is off the shop shelf. That closes the loop of "sell a crop, buy back the seed" — but it also removes the crop sale that used to fund the scarecrow and sprinkler, the only two things left in the shop that still cost gold (the robots are earned, not bought, under a separate ruling). This asks whether what fills that gap today — one settled number, the x3 harvest yield — gets the player to those purchases at a pace that still feels like farming, or whether the yield, the shipping bin's reserve, or the prices themselves need to move.

What the player experiences: every harvest hands back three plantable units instead of one. The player replants one and carries two spare. Those two spares go first into the shipping bin's reserve — ten of each species, kept for replanting rather than sold — and only once that reserve is full does a delivery start paying gold. A fresh farm's first full growing cycle (five starting wheat plant into fifteen units; five go back to replanting, ten fill the reserve) pays nothing. The next cycle, once the reserve stays full, starts paying up to 150g from ten excess wheat. Wheat takes three growing days; tomato, five.

Against today's prices — 25g coop, 50g scarecrow, 120g sprinkler — that means a quiet unpaid stretch while the reserve fills, then a much larger income. Without any harvest surplus at all, the player's only gold would be the hen's egg (roughly a coin flip each morning, 10g when it lands, about 5g/day on average): 10 mornings for the scarecrow alone, 24 more for the sprinkler. The x3 yield is meant to beat that egg-only floor by a wide margin once harvests start earning gold — the open question is whether the delay before harvests start earning gold is appropriate for a first-time player, or whether it reads as a period with no income.

Keeping today's numbers as they are changes no number — it accepts the current shape (one cycle fills the reserve, then later cycles produce more crops to sell) as the intended early-game progression, so scarecrow and sprinkler pricing can be tuned later from an actual playtest instead of from this arithmetic. Moving the yield or either price now would authorize a specific number to change before anyone has watched a real session hit it.
why_now: The x3 harvest yield (Q-115), the ten-unit carry cap (Q-113), and the shipping bin's ten-unit reserve (Q-116) have all been decided and included in the main version (`docs/SEED_ECONOMY_PLAN.md`); together they set the pace at which a player reaches the scarecrow and sprinkler, and nobody has decided whether that resulting pace is right. The prior analysis (`hq/data/work/w6ff2240c1fb.json`) flagged this as the real decision hiding inside the original harvest-as-seed request. The chosen pace changes how much gold the player actually has to spend in phase 1, which is why it needs your ruling before any of the three numbers move again.

options.label: Keep the x3 yield and today's prices; tune from a playtest (Recommended)
options.detail: Change nothing yet. The x3 yield already creates a renewable two-unit surplus per cycle where the old one-for-one yield created none, and the reserve's one-cycle delay is arithmetic, not a measured session. Watch when a real player actually reaches the scarecrow and sprinkler before moving either price.

options.label: Re-price the scarecrow and sprinkler down now
options.detail: Lower 50g and 120g to match the slower early pace without waiting for a playtest. Risks guessing wrong in either direction — too high still reads as a period with no income, too low makes the purchase feel free — and there is no observed session yet to aim at.

options.label: Raise the harvest yield above x3 now
options.detail: Give the first growing cycle sellable surplus too, instead of spending it entirely on filling the reserve. This reopens a number just settled two days ago (Q-115) on arithmetic alone, with no evidence the x3 figure itself is wrong — it only shortens the wait this question is asking about.
